collection.credit:
NEW EVENTS — HISTORY AND COLLECTIVE MEMORY (HIS-01..50, draft for the owner, 2026-11-15)
Old stories, ruins and abandoned places, heirlooms, disputed records, festivals that changed, names on carvings, customs nobody can explain, and the things a people remembers together: some of it painful and handled gently, some of it gloriously silly.
Written in the style of the owner's own events. Edit anything and send it back; nothing ships until you approve.

ledger.why: the casting line, carried out as the roles' ages (picks an adult and a child aged 6-13)

collection.description: A child wants to add a handprint to the old red handprints in the cave: let them add one, or keep the cave as it is.

setup.name: The setup
setup.text: In a dry cave above the beach, the walls are covered in old red handprints, blown around with paint so each hand shows up as a pale shape in a red cloud. Big hands and little hands, dozens of them. (friend) has been staring at them, and now (friend.he/she) wants to add (friend.his/her) own.

choices.label: Keep the Cave as It Is

o1.name: Outcome A
o1.text: (subject) hesitates, then agrees. They mix red earth and water in a shell. (friend) presses (friend.his/her) hand to a bare patch of wall, and (subject) blows the paint around it. When (friend.he/she) lifts it away, there's a small pale hand among all the old ones. (friend) can't stop looking at it. Someday, someone will wonder whose that one was.

o2.name: Outcome B
o2.text: (subject) says the cave belongs to the people who made those hands, and the walls should stay as they left them. (friend) is disappointed. Instead they go down to the beach, and (subject) helps (friend.him/her) make a handprint on a flat rock, with the same red paint. The sea will wash it away eventually. (friend) knows that, and seems to like it.
